mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when UNRATE < 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for UNRATE is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%) combined with moderate inflation (CPIAUCSL annualized growth < 2.5%) indicates a stable economic environment that supports positive equity returns by avoiding recessionary pressures and aggressive monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL growth < 2.5% (annualized) over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 3.0% and unemployment rate < 4.0%), a federal funds rate above 2.0% signals monetary tightening that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle regime (GDPC1 growth > 3.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS in this regime is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Positive payroll employment growth (PAYEMS annualized growth > 0.5%) indicates a strengthening labor market that increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO annualized growth > 0.5%) signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when INDPRO growth > 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for INDPRO is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.5% (indicating a prolonged low-rate environment) supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days by allowing time for monetary policy to stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS for 60-day returns is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1.2 million units signal strong consumer confidence and construction activity that supports economic growth and positive equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases when HOUST > 1.2 million over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for HOUST is < 0.03.
